analysis.title: Weekly Focus: Time for US midterms – and Democratic sweep?
key_insights: Major central banks (Fed, ECB, BOJ) kept rates on hold this week, as expected.
Oil traded in a USD 113-118 range as markets speculate about a renewed US attack on Iran after the midterms. European gas futures broke EUR 100/MWh for the first time since December 2022.
French 10-year yield stabilised below 5% after Moody's left France's rating unchanged last Friday.
Q3 earnings season is about halfway through and overall performance is solid. Large tech results were mixed and investor reception was weaker than revenue growth alone would suggest.
The investment boom looks intact: Taiwan Q3 GDP grew 14.4% y/y, and Taiwanese and South Korean exports continue to grow strongly.

Fed held at 3.75-4.00%. Market reaction was dovish, but Danske reads Warsh's comments on the outlook as hawkish. It maintains a call for 25bp hikes in December and March, with risks tilted to more hikes.

ECB held the deposit rate at 2.50%. Danske expects a 25bp hike to 2.75% in December, which Lagarde clearly signalled. Lagarde will step down early on 7 February 2027, with Klaas Knot and Pablo Hernández de Cos the two favourites to succeed her.

US midterms are on Tuesday. Tentative results are expected Wednesday morning but final results could take weeks. Polymarket gives Democrats a 69% chance of winning the Senate, and the House looks like a done deal for them.

Whether the US launches a new attack on Iran after the midterms is a key question for energy markets. It is not certain, as US interceptor stockpiles are depleted (CFR: 64% of Patriot and 40% of THAAD interceptors used) and replenishment will take years.
The Israeli election result was indecisive, so forming a government may be difficult and Netanyahu's caretaker government stays in charge in the meantime.

Next week's key data: China private PMIs, US ISM indices Monday and Tuesday (per the report text; the calendar lists ISM manufacturing Monday and ISM non-manufacturing Wednesday), the October US jobs report and Michigan survey on Friday, and euro area flash HICP on Wednesday.

Riksbank is expected to hike to 2.00% on Wednesday 4 November, with guidance keeping the door open for tightening without signalling a December hike. Norges Bank is expected to hold at 4.50% on Thursday, repeating its readiness to hike and keeping December alive.
Sweden: GDP 2.8% y/y, PPI rose to 11.2% y/y in September from 6.8%, and firms' price expectations point to larger-than-normal increases. Consumer confidence fell to 94.3.
Norway: seasonally adjusted unemployment is unchanged at 2.0%, and September retail sales fell 0.4%, with retail trade down more than 1% y/y.

Denmark: if France passes a budget with a deficit under 5% of GDP, EUR/DKK could rise toward 7.4760, which would trigger Danmarks Nationalbank intervention. No intervention in October would be a second month without intervention.
